# Canopticon

> Questions researched in depth, and articles written from what the research found. Every quote in an article links to the stored research document it came from. By Chris Telford. Licensed CC BY 4.0.

Feeds: https://canopticon.com/feed.xml (RSS), https://canopticon.com/feed.json (JSON Feed). Per-topic feeds live under https://canopticon.com/feeds/.

## McLuhan & media theory

- [Krasis](https://canopticon.com/Canopticon%20Paper%20Krasis.dc.html): The synthesis of the series. McLuhan said every medium changes the ratio among our senses; the paper series tests that literally, from ADHD and typing to drugs and addiction, and f
- [Exocrasis](https://canopticon.com/Canopticon%20Paper%20Exocrasis.dc.html): The computing environment, not the screen, is the medium: keyboard, memory, search and network move part of the configuration of the senses and of memory outside the body.
- [Heterocrasis](https://canopticon.com/Canopticon%20Paper%20Heterocrasis.dc.html): ADHD as a different starting balance of the senses. The strongest difference is in overall gain; the body and inner speech are mixed; binding is not looser.
- [Pharmakrasis](https://canopticon.com/Canopticon%20Paper%20Pharmakrasis.dc.html): Each class of drug sets its own balance of the senses — and the evidence for that is better than for any medium. When a drug meets a medium, as music does in psychedelic therapy, t
- [Narcocrasis](https://canopticon.com/Canopticon%20Paper%20Narcocrasis.dc.html): In dependence, what goes unseen is not the drug but the shifted baseline: the allostatic state is the medium, the drug its content. Two routes back — one turns the gain down, one m
- [Typomora](https://canopticon.com/Canopticon%20Paper%20Typomora.dc.html): McLuhan said electric media would bring back the voice. For fifty years computers made us type instead. The delay was the keyboard, not a mistake in the theory — and it is ending.
- [Sensory syncrasis](https://canopticon.com/Canopticon%20Paper%20Syncrasis.dc.html): McLuhan meant his "sense ratios" literally. The brain science he reached for failed; predictive processing now gives the idea a mechanism, a name and five tests.
- [Typomora: Neuroscience, Naming and Framing for Paper 3](https://canopticon.com/Canopticon%20Doc.dc.html?d=typomora-neuroscience-naming-and-framing-for-paper-3-the-typed-delay-a): The neuroscience: Literacy measurably changes the brain. Dehaene et al. (2010, Science) found increased responses to letters in the visual word form area (VWFA), a small displaceme
- [The Computing Environment and Sensory Syncrasis: Evidence Review for Paper 2](https://canopticon.com/Canopticon%20Doc.dc.html?d=the-computing-environment-and-sensory-syncrasis-evidence-review-for-pa): What the environment tunes toward: an outward-facing, fast-switching, offloaded mode. Readers calibrate less carefully and process expository text more shallowly on screens (g ≈ −0
- [Sensory Syncrasis Evidence Base: Screens (Paper A) and ADHD (Paper B)](https://canopticon.com/Canopticon%20Doc.dc.html?d=sensory-syncrasis-evidence-base-screens-paper-a-and-adhd-paper-b): Paper A (Screens): Change is real but mostly domain-specific and often enhancing. Action video games causally improve perceptual and attentional skills (Bediou et al. 2018: g = 0.3

- [The Medium Becomes the Ground: McLuhan and the Allostatic Model of Addiction (rebuilt)](https://canopticon.com/Canopticon%20Doc.dc.html?d=the-medium-becomes-the-ground-mcluhan-s-media-theory-and-the-allostati): Work linking McLuhan to drugs and addiction exists only at the level of discourse and metaphor. ## Attention & feeds

- [Paying to reach curious readers in 2026: ChatGPT ads, feed ads, paid newsletter recommendations, and the labelling rules](https://canopticon.com/articles/paying-to-reach-curious-readers-in-2026): ChatGPT now sells self-serve ads, but they cost about 3–8× more per impression than feed ads and are hard to measure, so the cheapest curious readers are still on Meta and Reddit. An ad can be the whole useful answer and still carry its label: the rules draw the line at fake people and hidden sponsors, not at ads that are worth reading.

## Video & design

- [Portraiture as a research method: Sara Lawrence-Lightfoot's "painting with words", how it differs from ethnography, and the case against it](https://canopticon.com/articles/portraiture-as-a-research-method): Portraiture puts the researcher's own judgement at the centre of a study and measures success by whether readers recognise the truth of the portrait, not by whether anyone could repeat it. Its sharpest critic says that leaves no way to check the portraitist; its founder's answer is that a visible self demands more discipline, not less.
- [How investigative YouTube video essays are built: the cold open, the late turn to meaning, and the channels that borrow the form without the evidence](https://canopticon.com/articles/how-investigative-youtube-video-essays-are-built): The strongest forensic video essays open on an artifact, walk through evidence in the order a viewer would experience it, and say what it all means only late in the video. That delayed turn is what persuades, which is why the same structure works just as well for channels whose evidence does not hold up.
- [The Documentary Voice: A Specification for Investigative/Forensic Production Type](https://canopticon.com/Canopticon%20Doc.dc.html?d=documentary-voice-specification-investigative-forensic-production-type): This report extracts operational guidelines for a "documentary" production type to sit alongside (and orthogonal to) the existing "video essay" type.
